label: Betonhallen (FUSE), Chalmers University of Technology
note: a large concrete hall; the authors write 'Betonhalllen (FUSE)' (params_room_Hall.py, SOFA RoomDescription), the label drops the third l (the Swedish spelling may be Betonghallen, not checked); typed industrial as a large hall that is not an acoustics laboratory; plan about 26.0 x 23.8 m from the hand sketch (Room Hall - Dimensions.jpg), height not given; a commented calculation in the authors' x2_Gather_And_Plot_Measurements.m (lines 37-41) puts the loudspeakers 9.23 m from the receiver, horizontally, the high one at 4.62 m (floor 0.26 m, ear height 1.23 m), for elevations of about +20 and -6 degrees; the authors used a 5 s sweep and a 2.5 s deconvolution window here against 2 s and 0.5 s in the lab (params_room_*.py), and the published IRs are 1.23 s long (the lab's 0.21 s); the 18-microphone array here is XMA18v2 (50 dB pre-amp gain); sources are the loudspeaker heights

label: Anechoic chamber, Chalmers University of Technology
note: free-field reference, outside room statistics: KEMAR, the spherical array and the 18-microphone array (360 orientations) for one loudspeaker at ear height; both XMA18 and XMA18v2 are read: the same microphones and dummy head with 40 dB pre-amp gain (the lab's configuration) and 50 dB (the hall's), v2 recorded in a separate session (file dated 11 May 2023, v1 14 February; air 23-24 C and 36-37 % against 25 C and 45 %) and processed with a 22 kHz deconvolution low-pass; after gain and lag alignment they still differ by about -6.6 dB (median), against -14.6 dB between orientations 1 degree apart, so they are two measurements, not one scaled, and the authors use both as calibration sets; the authors removed the loudspeaker response from every anechoic set (and the microphone response from the arrays) and added a low-frequency extension (x2_Gather_And_Plot_Measurements.m, third configuration), while in the lab and hall only the array IRs are equalised for their microphones
